# Inheritance Introduction

#### Course: Learn Java OOP

## Inheritance Introduction

In the last chapter, we learned about object-oriented programming in Java. In this chapter, we will learn about Inheritance which is one of the important concepts of OOP.

Let's consider a scenario to understand what inheritance is and what problem it solves.

### Why Inheritance?

Suppose we need to create a racing game with cars and motorcycles as vehicles.

To solve this problem, we can create two separate classes to handle each of their functionalities.

However, both cars and motorcycles are vehicles and they will share some common fields and methods.

So instead of creating two independent classes, we can create the Vehicle class that shares the common features of both cars and motorcycles. Then, we can derive the Car class from the Vehicle class.

In doing so, the Car class inherits all the fields and methods of the Vehicle class. And, we can add car-specific features in the Car class as well.

Similarly, we can derive the Motorcycle class that inherits from the Vehicle class. Again, this Motorcycle class gets all vehicle-specific fields and methods from the Vehicle class.

![Java Inheritance](data:image/png;base64,)

This is the basic concept of inheritance. Inheritance allows a class (subclass) to inherit fields and methods from another class (superclass).

In our example, Vehicle is the superclass. Also known as the parent or base class and Car and Motorcycle are subclasses. Also known as the child or derived classes.

Next, we will learn to implement inheritance in Java.
